audit_status.source_base: Hebrew source via Sefaria with source/English versification reconciliation; public-domain KJV familiar comparison
audit_status.review_note: Draft restoration of 2 Chronicles 10 matching KJV numbering. Preserves Hebrew textures (metaphor, divine causation) and renders divine name as YHWH; requires witness-check on a few phrases.

verses.restored: Rehoboam went to Shechem; for all Israel had come to Shechem to make him king.

familiar.text: And Rehoboam went to Shechem: for to Shechem were all Israel come to make him king.

modern.text: Then Rehoboam went to Shechem, for all Israel had gone there to make him king.

original.text: וַיֵּ֥לֶךְ רְחַבְעָ֖ם שְׁכֶ֑מָה כִּ֥י שְׁכֶ֛ם בָּ֥אוּ כָל יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל לְהַמְלִ֥יךְ אֹתֽוֹ

verses.restored: And it came to pass, when Jeroboam son of Nebat, who had been in Egypt—where he had fled from Solomon the king—heard, that Jeroboam returned from Egypt.

familiar.text: And it came to pass, when Jeroboam the son of Nebat, who was in Egypt, whither he had fled from the presence of Solomon the king, heard it, that Jeroboam returned out of Egypt.

modern.text: When Jeroboam son of Nebat heard about this, he returned from Egypt, where he had fled from King Solomon.

original.text: וַיְהִ֞י כִּשְׁמֹ֨עַ יָרָבְעָ֤ם בֶּן נְבָט֙ וְה֣וּא בְמִצְרַ֔יִם אֲשֶׁ֣ר בָּרַ֔ח מִפְּנֵ֖י שְׁלֹמֹ֣ה הַמֶּ֑לֶךְ וַיָּ֥שָׁב יָרָבְעָ֖ם מִמִּצְרָֽיִם

verses.restored: They sent and called him; so Jeroboam and all Israel came and spoke to Rehoboam, saying,

familiar.text: And they sent and called him. So Jeroboam and all Israel came and spake to Rehoboam, saying,

modern.text: So they sent for Jeroboam, and he and all Israel came to Rehoboam and said,

original.text: וַֽיִּשְׁלְחוּ֙ וַיִּקְרְאוּ ל֔וֹ וַיָּבֹ֥א יָרָבְעָ֖ם וְכָל יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל וַֽיְדַבְּר֔וּ אֶל רְחַבְעָ֖ם לֵאמֹֽר

verses.restored: "Thy father made our yoke grievous; now therefore ease somewhat the grievous service of thy father and the heavy yoke he put upon us, and we will serve thee."

familiar.text: Thy father made our yoke grievous: now therefore ease thou somewhat the grievous servitude of thy father, and his heavy yoke that he put upon us, and we will serve thee.

modern.text: “Your father put a heavy yoke on us. But now you should lighten the burden of your father’s service and the heavy yoke he put on us, and we will serve you.”

original.text: אָבִ֖יךָ הִקְשָׁ֣ה אֶת עֻלֵּ֑נוּ וְעַתָּ֡ה הָקֵל֩ מֵעֲבֹדַ֨ת אָבִ֜יךָ הַקָּשָׁ֗ה וּמֵעֻלּ֧וֹ הַכָּבֵ֛ד אֲשֶׁר נָתַ֥ן עָלֵ֖ינוּ וְנַֽעַבְדֶֽךָּ

verses.restored: He said unto them, "Come again to me after three days." And the people departed.

familiar.text: And he said unto them, Come again unto me after three days. And the people departed.

modern.text: Rehoboam answered, “Come back to me in three days.” So the people departed.

original.text: וַיֹּ֣אמֶר אֲלֵהֶ֗ם ע֛וֹד שְׁלֹ֥שֶׁת יָמִ֖ים וְשׁ֣וּבוּ אֵלָ֑י וַיֵּ֖לֶךְ הָעָֽם

verses.restored: The king consulted the elders who had stood before Solomon his father while he yet lived, saying, "How counsel ye that I should answer this people?"

familiar.text: And king Rehoboam took counsel with the old men that had stood before Solomon his father while he yet lived, saying, What counsel give ye me to return answer to this people?

modern.text: Then King Rehoboam consulted with the elders who had served his father Solomon during his lifetime. “How do you advise me to respond to these people?” he asked.

original.text: וַיִּוָּעַ֞ץ הַמֶּ֣לֶךְ רְחַבְעָ֗ם אֶת הַזְּקֵנִים֙ אֲשֶׁר הָי֣וּ עֹֽמְדִ֗ים לִפְנֵי֙ שְׁלֹמֹ֣ה אָבִ֔יו בִּֽהְיֹת֥וֹ חַ֖י לֵאמֹ֑ר אֵ֚יךְ אַתֶּ֣ם נֽוֹעָצִ֔ים לְהָשִׁ֥יב לָֽעָם הַזֶּ֖ה דָּבָֽר

verses.restored: And they spake unto him, "If thou be kind to this people, and please them, and speak good words to them, they will be thy servants for ever."

familiar.text: And they spake unto him, saying, If thou be kind to this people, and please them, and speak good words to them, they will be thy servants for ever.

modern.text: They replied, “If you will be kind to these people and please them by speaking kind words to them, they will be your servants forever.”

original.text: וַיְדַבְּר֨וּ אֵלָ֜יו לֵאמֹ֗ר אִם תִּֽהְיֶ֨ה לְט֜וֹב לְהָעָ֤ם הַזֶּה֙ וּרְצִיתָ֔ם וְדִבַּרְתָּ֥ אֲלֵהֶ֖ם דְּבָרִ֣ים טוֹבִ֑ים וְהָי֥וּ לְךָ֛ עֲבָדִ֖ים כָּל הַיָּמִֽים

verses.restored: But he forsook the counsel of the elders and took counsel with the young men that were brought up with him, who stood before him.

familiar.text: But he forsook the counsel which the old men gave him, and took counsel with the young men that were brought up with him, that stood before him.

modern.text: But Rehoboam rejected the advice of the elders; instead, he consulted the young men who had grown up with him and served him.

original.text: וַֽיַּעֲזֹ֛ב אֶת עֲצַ֥ת הַזְּקֵנִ֖ים אֲשֶׁ֣ר יְעָצֻ֑הוּ וַיִּוָּעַ֗ץ אֶת הַיְלָדִים֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר גָּדְל֣וּ אִתּ֔וֹ הָעֹמְדִ֖ים לְפָנָֽיו

verses.restored: He said unto them, "What counsel give ye that we may return answer to this people, which have spoken to me, saying, 'Ease somewhat the yoke that thy father did put upon us' ?"

familiar.text: And he said unto them, What advice give ye that we may return answer to this people, which have spoken to me, saying, Ease somewhat the yoke that thy father did put upon us?

modern.text: He asked them, “What message do you advise that we send back to these people who have spoken to me, saying, ‘Lighten the yoke your father put on us’?”

original.text: וַיֹּ֣אמֶר אֲלֵהֶ֗ם מָ֚ה אַתֶּ֣ם נֽוֹעָצִ֔ים וְנָשִׁ֥יב דָּבָ֖ר אֶת הָעָ֣ם הַזֶּ֑ה אֲשֶׁ֨ר דִּבְּר֤וּ אֵלַי֙ לֵאמֹ֔ר הָקֵל֙ מִן הָעֹ֔ל אֲשֶׁר נָתַ֥ן אָבִ֖יךָ עָלֵֽינוּ

verses.restored: The young men that were brought up with him spake unto him, "Thus shalt thou say to the people that have spoken to thee, 'Thy father made our yoke heavy, but make thou it lighter for us' — thus shalt thou say unto them: 'My little finger shall be thicker than my father's loins.'"

familiar.text: And the young men that were brought up with him spake unto him, saying, Thus shalt thou answer the people that spake unto thee, saying, Thy father made our yoke heavy, but make thou it somewhat lighter for us; thus shalt thou say unto them, My little finger shall be thicker than my father’s loins.

modern.text: The young men who had grown up with him replied, “This is how you should answer these people who said to you, ‘Your father made our yoke heavy, but you should make it lighter.’ This is what you should tell them: ‘My little finger is thicker than my father’s waist!

original.text: וַיְדַבְּר֣וּ אִתּ֗וֹ הַיְלָדִים֙ אֲשֶׁ֨ר גָּדְל֣וּ אִתּוֹ֮ לֵאמֹר֒ כֹּֽה תֹאמַ֡ר לָעָם֩ אֲשֶׁר דִּבְּר֨וּ אֵלֶ֜יךָ לֵאמֹ֗ר אָבִ֨יךָ֙ הִכְבִּ֣יד אֶת עֻלֵּ֔נוּ וְאַתָּ֖ה הָקֵ֣ל מֵעָלֵ֑ינוּ כֹּ֚ה תֹּאמַ֣ר אֲלֵהֶ֔ם קָֽטָנִּ֥י עָבָ֖ה מִמָּתְנֵ֥י אָבִֽי

verses.restored: "For whereas my father put a heavy yoke upon you, I will add to your yoke; my father chastised you with whips, but I will chastise you with scorpions."

familiar.text: For whereas my father put a heavy yoke upon you, I will put more to your yoke: my father chastised you with whips, but I will chastise you with scorpions.

notes.title: short
notes.body: Hebrew metaphor עַקְרַבִּים ('akravim') preserved as 'scorpions'—image of harsher corporal punishment.

modern.text: Whereas my father burdened you with a heavy yoke, I will add to your yoke. Whereas my father scourged you with whips, I will scourge you with scorpions.’”

original.text: וְעַתָּ֗ה אָבִי֙ הֶעְמִ֤יס עֲלֵיכֶם֙ עֹ֣ל כָּבֵ֔ד וַאֲנִ֖י אֹסִ֣יף עַֽל עֻלְּכֶ֑ם אָבִ֗י יִסַּ֤ר אֶתְכֶם֙ בַּשּׁוֹטִ֔ים וַאֲנִ֖י בָּֽעֲקְרַבִּֽים

verses.restored: So Jeroboam and all the people came to Rehoboam on the third day, as the king had appointed, saying, "Come again to me on the third day."

familiar.text: So Jeroboam and all the people came to Rehoboam on the third day, as the king bade, saying, Come again to me on the third day.

modern.text: After three days, Jeroboam and all the people returned to Rehoboam, since the king had said, “Come back to me on the third day.”

original.text: וַיָּבֹ֨א יָרָבְעָ֧ם וְכָל הָעָ֛ם אֶל רְחַבְעָ֖ם בַּיּ֣וֹם הַשְּׁלִשִׁ֑י כַּאֲשֶׁ֨ר דִּבֶּ֤ר הַמֶּ֨לֶךְ֙ לֵאמֹ֔ר שׁ֥וּבוּ אֵלַ֖י בַּיּ֥וֹם הַשְּׁלִשִֽׁי

verses.restored: And the king answered them roughly; and Rehoboam forsook the counsel of the elders.

familiar.text: And the king answered them roughly; and king Rehoboam forsook the counsel of the old men,

modern.text: And the king answered them harshly. King Rehoboam rejected the advice of the elders

original.text: וַיַּעֲנֵ֥ם הַמֶּ֖לֶךְ קָשָׁ֑ה וַֽיַּעֲזֹב֙ הַמֶּ֣לֶךְ רְחַבְעָ֔ם אֵ֖ת עֲצַ֥ת הַזְּקֵנִֽים

verses.restored: And he answered them after the counsel of the young men, saying, 'My father made your yoke heavy, but I will add thereto; my father chastised you with whips, but I will chastise you with scorpions.'

familiar.text: And answered them after the advice of the young men, saying, My father made your yoke heavy, but I will add thereto: my father chastised you with whips, but I will chastise you with scorpions.

modern.text: and spoke to them as the young men had advised, saying, “Whereas my father made your yoke heavy, I will add to your yoke. Whereas my father scourged you with whips, I will scourge you with scorpions.”

original.text: וַיְדַבֵּ֣ר אֲלֵהֶ֗ם כַּעֲצַ֤ת הַיְלָדִים֙ לֵאמֹ֔ר אַכְבִּיד֙ אֶֽת עֻלְּכֶ֔ם וַאֲנִ֖י אֹסִ֣יף עָלָ֑יו אָבִ֗י יִסַּ֤ר אֶתְכֶם֙ בַּשּׁוֹטִ֔ים וַאֲנִ֖י בָּעֲקְרַבִּֽים

verses.restored: So the king hearkened not unto the people; for the matter was from YHWH, to fulfil his word which he spoke by the hand of Ahijah the Shilonite to Jeroboam son of Nebat.

familiar.text: So the king hearkened not unto the people: for the cause was of God, that the LORD might perform his word, which he spake by the hand of Ahijah the Shilonite to Jeroboam the son of Nebat.

notes.title: short
notes.body: Hebrew states the cause as from YHWH; preserves prophetic fulfillment via Ahijah (אֲחִיָּהוּ).

modern.text: So the king did not listen to the people, and indeed this turn of events was from God, in order that the LORD might fulfill the word that He had spoken through Ahijah the Shilonite to Jeroboam son of Nebat. The Kingdom Divided (1 Kings 12:16–19)

original.text: וְלֹֽא שָׁמַ֥ע הַמֶּ֖לֶךְ אֶל הָעָ֑ם כִּֽי הָיְתָ֤ה נְסִבָּה֙ מֵעִ֣ם הָֽאֱלֹהִ֔ים לְמַעַן֩ הָקִ֨ים יְהוָ֜ה אֶת דְּבָר֗וֹ אֲשֶׁ֤ר דִּבֶּר֙ בְּיַד֙ אֲחִיָּ֣הוּ הַשִּֽׁלוֹנִ֔י אֶל יָרָבְעָ֖ם בֶּן נְבָֽט

verses.restored: And when all Israel saw that the king would not hearken unto them, the people answered the king, 'What portion have we in David? and we have no inheritance in the son of Jesse. Every man to your tents, O Israel: now see to thine own house, David.' So all Israel went to their tents.

familiar.text: And when all Israel saw that the king would not hearken unto them, the people answered the king, saying, What portion have we in David? and we have none inheritance in the son of Jesse: every man to your tents, O Israel: and now, David, see to thine own house. So all Israel went to their tents.

modern.text: When all Israel saw that the king had refused to listen to them, they answered the king: “What portion do we have in David, and what inheritance in the son of Jesse? To your tents, O Israel! Look now to your own house, O David!” So all the Israelites went home,

original.text: וְכָל יִשְׂרָאֵ֗ל כִּ֠י לֹא שָׁמַ֣ע הַמֶּלֶךְ֮ לָהֶם֒ וַיָּשִׁ֣יבוּ הָעָ֣ם אֶת הַמֶּ֣לֶךְ לֵאמֹ֡ר מַה לָּנוּ֩ חֵ֨לֶק בְּדָוִ֜יד וְלֹֽא נַחֲלָ֣ה בְּבֶן יִשַׁ֗י אִ֤ישׁ לְאֹהָלֶ֨יךָ֙ יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל עַתָּ֕ה רְאֵ֥ה בֵיתְךָ֖ דָּוִ֑יד וַיֵּ֥לֶךְ כָּל יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל לְאֹהָלָֽיו

verses.restored: But as for the Israelites who dwelt in the cities of Judah, Rehoboam reigned over them.

familiar.text: But as for the children of Israel that dwelt in the cities of Judah, Rehoboam reigned over them.

modern.text: but Rehoboam still reigned over the Israelites living in the cities of Judah.

original.text: וּבְנֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל הַיֹּֽשְׁבִ֖ים בְּעָרֵ֣י יְהוּדָ֑ה וַיִּמְלֹ֥ךְ עֲלֵיהֶ֖ם רְחַבְעָֽם

verses.restored: Then king Rehoboam sent Hadoram who was over the levy; and the children of Israel stoned him with stones, and he died. And the king made speed to get him up into his chariot to flee to Jerusalem.

familiar.text: Then king Rehoboam sent Hadoram that was over the tribute; and the children of Israel stoned him with stones, that he died. But king Rehoboam made speed to get him up to his chariot, to flee to Jerusalem.

modern.text: Then King Rehoboam sent out Hadoram, who was in charge of the forced labor, but the Israelites stoned him to death. And King Rehoboam mounted his chariot in haste and escaped to Jerusalem.

original.text: וַיִּשְׁלַ֞ח הַמֶּ֣לֶךְ רְחַבְעָ֗ם אֶת הֲדֹרָם֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר עַל הַמַּ֔ס וַיִּרְגְּמוּ ב֧וֹ בְנֵֽי יִשְׂרָאֵ֛ל אֶ֖בֶן וַיָּמֹ֑ת וְהַמֶּ֣לֶךְ רְחַבְעָ֗ם הִתְאַמֵּץ֙ לַֽעֲל֣וֹת בַּמֶּרְכָּבָ֔ה לָנ֖וּס יְרוּשָׁלִָֽם

verses.restored: And Israel rebelled against the house of David unto this day.

familiar.text: And Israel rebelled against the house of David unto this day.

modern.text: So to this day Israel has been in rebellion against the house of David.

original.text: וַיִּפְשְׁע֤וּ יִשְׂרָאֵל֙ בְּבֵ֣ית דָּוִ֔יד עַ֖ד הַיּ֥וֹם הַזֶּֽה

translation_notes: Divine name יהוה rendered YHWH throughout; KJV verse numbering preserved though Hebrew chapters were reconciled from supplied context.
Metaphor עַקְרַבִּים rendered 'scorpions' as source-sensitive figurative punishments; preserved rhetorical image 'my little finger...'.
Speech acts and abrupt register shifts preserved; minimal smoothing to retain source difficulty.
safety_note: This chapter contains violence and punitive rhetoric presented as in source; handle with care in sensitive contexts.
